text:
lauryn (PM): FYI BigCorp opened a ticket: after a catalog rotation their similarity recall tanked. They want a formal migration path + a promise around embedding schema stability. Need product wording for legal + a short-term mitigation.

nate (eng): can we confirm whether its dim change, dtype, or just normalization differences?

mei (applied-ml): inspected sample: dims went 1024 -> 768 and distribution shifted (mean moved, L2 norms different). So both dim + normalization.

lauryn (PM): customer asks: (A) guarantee that major schema-breaking swaps will have a 30d notice and compatibility options; (B) tooling to avoid full reindexing immediately.

sara (acct): contract currently says "reasonable notice". Legal wants explicit grace window and mitigation options to avoid credits. Need text.

ryan (devex): we can build: 1) a server-side adapter (pad/truncate + optional PCA-up/down projection), 2) a pin-by-catalog-version option, 3) a migration job endpoint that re-embeds asynchronously. CLI: `ri-migrate run --customer C --from m_old --to m_new --mode reindex|shim|pin`.

nate (eng): engineering tradeoffs: shim is cheap but can mask semantic shifts. PCA projection can be lossy but better than zero-pad sometimes. Keeping both models live increases cost but simplest for customers.

mei (applied-ml): recommend we require a small evaluation harness: given customer seed queries and their index subset, compute top-k overlap, MRR, and cosine shift. Define thresholds: soft alert if MRR drop >3%, block rollout if >8% without explicit waiver.

lauryn (PM): propose policy: for enterprise customers default is 30d gracepath + default pin_old. During gracepath we offer adapter (auto_adapter) or scheduled reindex. If customer picks auto_adapter we run weekly regression checks and show pass/fail in console.

sara (acct): customers will want the opt-in explicit in console and contract; also a log that they accepted auto-adapter tradeoffs.

ryan (devex): mock API payload for opt-in: `{ "compat_mode": "auto_adapter|pin_old|reindex_schedule", "grace_period_days": "30", "compatibility_check_id": "uuid" }`. We'll surface `embed_schema` in model manifest: `{ "dim": "1024", "dtype": "float32", "schema_version": "e2" }`.

nate (eng): quick pseudocode for PCA-based downsample (can be toggled):```python
# assume V_new: (n, D_new), target D_old
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
pca = PCA(n_components=D_old)
V_projected = pca.fit_transform(V_new)
# renormalize per vector
V_proj = V_projected / np.linalg.norm(V_projected, axis=1, keepdims=True)
```

mei (applied-ml): also offer an asymmetric mapping option: map old->new or new->old depending on which preserves retrieval better. We'll include a `compat.direction` field.

lauryn (PM): metrics to expose: `compat.applied_count`, `compat.rollback_count`, `compat.mrr_delta_weekly`, and `catalog.schema_change_requests`. Also surface a per-customer `compatibility_check` report artifact link.

ryan (devex): docs + CLI: `ri-compat diff --old m1 --new m2 --sample sample.json --metrics mrr,overlap` -> outputs a report with PDF and JSON artifacts. We'll add example output.

sara (acct): i'll draft contract language: "For enterprise customers, Redwood will provide a 30-day grace period for schema-incompatible embedding version changes. During the grace period, customers may elect pinning to the previous model, an automated compatibility adapter, or schedule a full reindex. Redwood will provide a compatibility report and run weekly regressions; if regressions exceed agreed thresholds, Redwood will fallback to the pinned model until resolved." Thoughts?

nate (eng): add: "Redwood will make best-effort to provide adapter behavior but does not guarantee parity of semantic retrieval when structural schema changes occur."

mei (applied-ml): add gating in catalog onboarding: any model with differing dim or dtype must include: a compatibility matrix, eval harness results vs canonical baselines, recommended adapter mapping, and an explicit schema_version bump entry.

lauryn (PM): OK. Next steps: 1) eng: implement shim + canary route (nate) 2) devex: CLI + diff report (ryan) 3) applied-ml: eval harness + thresholds (mei) 4) acct/legal: contract language + customer opt-in UI (sara).

infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled: feature/embed-compat -> canary 5% on 2026-03-23T04:00Z

ryan (devex): i'll prototype the `ri-compat diff` output JSON schema and a sample HTML report for BigCorp. Need sample index subset (~10k vectors) from them.

sara (acct): requesting sample now. Also flagging priority = high for the ticket.

lauryn (PM): i'll update the model-catalog checklist: add "Embedding Schema Stability" section with required fields: required_dim, dtype, schema_version, compat_options, grace_period_days, regression_thresholds, and required artifacts link. Dropping into the catalog PR after eng MVP.

nate (eng): question: do we force a manual catalog approval step for any schema_version increment?

mei (applied-ml): yes for major changes (dim/dtype). minor normalization updates can go through automated compatibility-check + opt-in.

lauryn (PM): agreed. i'll capture that as a hard gating in the onboarding playbook. Thanks everyone.
